goal: Land the MessagingAdapter seam with EmailAdapter (Resend) as its first implementation, the domain-scoped solicitation sending identity and its four config vars with a boot assertion, the getEmailHeaders 'solicitation' category that throws on a missing unsubscribe URL, and the tag-discriminated solicitation lane in the Resend webhook ingress that records bounce/complaint/provider-suppressed facts onto the Outreach row and the Suppression ledger.
non_goals: Any migration — 091 already carries provider_message_id, bounced_at, complained_at, unsubscribed_at, and the four new env vars are config not schema

An index on solicitation_outreach.provider_message_id — 091 created none; the table has zero rows until #630 sends, so the index ships with the volume in #630 (owner decision 2026-08-16, follow-up filed)

solicitation_outreach.delivered_at — the column does not exist and spec §5.3's delivered_at effect is dropped; 091's own comment locks the async signals as 'columns, NOT statuses (D13)' (owner decision 2026-08-16)

Writing solicitation_outreach.unsubscribed_at — the RFC 8058 POST terminates on worker/ingress/unsubscribe.ts (#644), not the Resend webhook, so no event in this lane can set it
Actually dispatching an ask — #630 owns the drip worker, the unsubscribe token mint at dispatch (amendment B4), and the dispatch-time postal-address byte-match
Reputation circuit breaker (spec §3.2B) — deferred entirely to #630, which owns the health-window read model, the latch, the admin reset and the gate together
Per-account and platform daily cap ENFORCEMENT — this ticket registers and boot-asserts SOLICITATION_PLATFORM_DAILY_CAP and enforces nothing
Creating the Resend domains or the Cloudflare DNS records — the runbook is authored here, executed at #633
Changing the existing notification_deliveries webhook path — it stays byte-for-byte unchanged
Pushing anything to Resend's suppression API — spec §6.2, it is team-wide across every domain and key including transactional
Automating reply-based opt-out capture from the reviews@ mailbox — spec FU-4
Moving transactional off the apex to notify.repworth.net — spec FU-1, invariant #3 blast radius
user_visible_behavior: No owner-visible or recipient-visible behavior changes: the feature lands inert because SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED is off in every environment and no Outreach row carries a provider_message_id until #630 sends

An operator who sets SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED=true without all four solicitation config vars gets a worker that refuses to boot with a message naming the missing vars, instead of a worker that fails at dispatch time
A Resend webhook whose data.tags.lane is 'solicitation' is routed to the solicitation lane before any DB lookup; every other payload reaches the existing notification_deliveries path unchanged
invariants: Invariant #6: third-party ingress terminates on Railway — the solicitation lane lives in worker/ingress/, never proxied through Next.js
Invariant #3 reached sideways is closed by the key split: a leaked SOLICITATION_RESEND_API_KEY cannot send transactional mail, so it cannot forge an approval email
Invariant #5 reached sideways is closed the same way — a solicitation-lane key cannot mint or deliver an approval link
Invariant #13: all four config vars are server-only with no NEXT_PUBLIC_* companion, enforced by ci:static-policy

extractBounceType, isHardBounceType and classifyBounce are reused verbatim — a second classifier would be a second owner of 'what counts as permanent', and 'unknown'-classifies-as-soft is the correct fail-safe in this lane too
recordSuppression in src/lib/solicitation/suppression.ts stays the single owner of the byte-for-byte ON CONFLICT predicates; the lane calls it and never re-spells them

Every solicitation config var fails closed: unset means no solicitation sends, never a degraded send
The suppression write and the Outreach-row signal write for one event commit in ONE transaction
Signature verification, claimInboundEvent idempotency, the 503-retry contract and the stale-svix-timestamp window are unchanged and reused by both lanes
edge_cases: A webhook payload carries lane=solicitation but its provider_message_id matches no Outreach row — the response splits by event (D1/F1): observability-only events (soft or unknown bounce, email.failed) take a structured warn and ack 200, while suppression-bearing events (permanent bounce, complaint, provider-suppressed) throw so the handler returns 503 and Resend retries into #630's provider_message_id commit window. Either way NO suppression is written; we never suppress a handle we cannot attribute
A webhook payload carries no tags at all — it reaches the existing notification_deliveries path, exactly as today
A payload's tags are an array of {name,value} rather than an object — the lane discriminant must read Resend's actual echoed shape, not an assumed one
email.bounced with a Temporary or unknown bounce type — bounced_at and provider_error are recorded, and NO suppression is written
email.bounced with a Permanent type — bounced_at recorded and a bounce_permanent global Suppression ledger row written in the same transaction
email.complained — complained_at recorded and a complaint global Suppression ledger row written in the same transaction
email.suppressed — a provider_suppressed global Suppression ledger row plus a loud log; there is no Outreach column for it, and it means Resend's team-wide list is diverging from ours
email.failed records failed.reason into provider_error and never suppresses
email.delivery_delayed, email.sent and email.delivered are ack-and-log only in this lane
email.opened, email.clicked, email.scheduled and email.received reach the lane — they are refused, not crashed on

provider_error is already populated by #630's dispatch failure — the webhook preserves it rather than overwriting, matching the #736 Watchdog rule that a bounded error class survives a generic reclaim
A duplicate webhook for an already-suppressed handle — recordSuppression is first-write-wins, so the second is a no-op and mints no duplicate analytics event
A duplicate svix-id — claimInboundEvent returns duplicate and both lanes ack 200 without reprocessing
The suppression write throws — the whole event fails, markInboundEventFailed records it, and the handler returns 503 so Resend retries
getEmailHeaders('solicitation') is called with no unsubscribeUrl — it throws; it never falls back to LIST_UNSUBSCRIBE_URL and never to the repworth.example.com RFC 2606 mailbox
getEmailHeaders('solicitation') is called with a non-HTTPS unsubscribeUrl — it throws rather than silently degrading to a mailto-only header
SOLICITATION_RESEND_API_KEY is unset and something asks for the solicitation client — it throws, so an unset key can never fall through to the transactional client
SOLICITATION_PLATFORM_DAILY_CAP is set to an unparseable value with SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED on — boot fails; presence alone is not enough
SOLICITATION_PLATFORM_DAILY_CAP is explicitly 0 with the flag on — boot succeeds; 0 is the warm-up dial at rest, not a misconfiguration
MOCK_EXTERNAL_APIS=true with SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED on — the boot assertion no-ops, matching assertChannelsWhatsAppEnv
The adapter is asked to send to more than one recipient — refused; exactly one recipient per message, because each ask carries its own token, consent re-check and Outreach row
The adapter is asked to send without a plain-text part — refused; HTML-only is a meaningful spam signal and multipart is always required

rollback_plan: Revert the PR. There is NO migration — the four config vars are Railway env only and every one fails closed, so an environment that never sets them is byte-identical before and after. The feature is unreachable in prod either way: SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED is off everywhere, and no Outreach row carries a provider_message_id until #630 sends, so the webhook lane's discriminant can never match. Order: ride staging with the flag OFF, confirm the existing notification_deliveries webhook path is unaffected, then merge to main. To back out at runtime WITHOUT a revert, unset SOLICITATION_RESEND_API_KEY AND RESTART THE WORKER — getSolicitationResend caches its client and getServerConfig is memoized, so an already-booted worker keeps the authorized client until it restarts; on Railway an env change triggers a redeploy, which restarts it. (Corrected 2026-08-16 after plan-review finding F4: the original wording claimed the unset alone stopped sends, which is false in-process. Recorded in the deviations file.) The webhook lane stays live and harmless either way — per glossary rule DR1 the flag masters sending only. Reverting the code while the four vars remain set in Railway is also safe: no reverted code reads them.
observability: One structured log line per solicitation webhook event from createWorkerLogger, carrying event type, outreach id, account_id, business_id and the classified bounce reason — and never the recipient address or message body. This is the signal that the lane is receiving and attributing events at all.
A loud warn on email.suppressed, because it means Resend's team-wide suppression list is diverging from our ledger (spec §6.2) and an admin needs to look.

A structured warn on an unmatched provider_message_id under lane=solicitation — a sustained rate means the tag is being emitted for sends we are not recording, which is the failure that would silently lose bounce and complaint facts.
A boot failure naming the missing solicitation env vars is itself the signal for a misconfigured worker: the worker refusing to start is louder than a worker that starts and fails at dispatch.

The Suppression ledger is the durable record — querying solicitation_suppressions by source for bounce_permanent, complaint and provider_suppressed answers 'is the webhook lane working' directly, with no derived state to drift.
